scenes.heading: Adding and subtracting integers
scenes.say: Negative fifteen plus twenty-eight minus nine, minus negative six, plus negative twelve. Looks scary? In this video you'll learn a tidy way to handle long strings of positive and negative numbers.
scenes.caption: −15 + 28 − 9 − (−6) + (−12). Looks scary? In this video you'll learn a tidy way to handle long strings of positive and negative numbers.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A tipping scoreboard: add up all the gains, add up all the losses
scenes.science: Gather the positives, gather the negatives, then compare the totals
scenes.breaks: a scoreboard never subtracts a negative, so tidy any double signs first.
scenes.say: Picture a footy tipping scoreboard. You gain points for right tips and lose points for wrong ones. You don't need to replay every game: add the gains, add the losses, and compare. Long integer sums work the same way. Just remember to tidy any double signs first.

scenes.heading: Tidy, gather, compare
points: Each sign stays with the number after it
Gather: add the positives, add the negatives
Compare: the bigger total gives the sign
scenes.say: Here's the method. Tidy: two signs the same make plus, two different make minus. Remember each sign rides with the number after it. Gather: add up the positives and add up the negatives. Compare: find the difference, and the bigger total decides the sign.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Work out −15 + 28 − 9 − (−6) + (−12).
scenes.say: Tidy the signs first: minus negative six becomes plus six, and plus negative twelve becomes minus twelve. Positives: twenty-eight plus six is thirty-four. Negatives: fifteen plus nine plus twelve is thirty-six. The negatives win by two, so the answer is negative two.
scenes.caption: Tidy: −15 + 28 − 9 + 6 − 12. Positives: 28 + 6 = 34. Negatives: 15 + 9 + 12 = 36. The negatives win by 2, so the answer is −2.

scenes.heading: A change on the number line
notes: The jump is 13 to the right
scenes.say: First the number line, then a dot at the start, negative four. The temperature ends at nine, so we jump to the right all the way to nine. That jump is thirteen steps, and it goes right, so the change is plus thirteen. Nine minus negative four gives the same answer.
scenes.caption: Start at −4 and finish at 9. The jump is 13 to the right, so the change is +13. 9 − (−4) gives the same answer.

scenes.heading: Working out a change
scenes.say: To find a change, always do final minus start. A positive change means it went up. A negative change means it went down.

scenes.heading: A change below sea level
scenes.question: A submarine moves from −135 m to −62 m. What is the change?
scenes.say: A submarine moves from negative one hundred and thirty-five metres to negative sixty-two metres. Change equals final minus start: negative sixty-two minus negative one hundred and thirty-five. Change two signs: negative sixty-two plus one hundred and thirty-five, which is seventy-three. Positive, so it went up seventy-three metres.
scenes.caption: −62 − (−135) = −62 + 135 = 73. Positive, so it went up 73 m.

points: Gather positives and negatives, then compare
Missing number? Use the inverse, then check
scenes.say: Quick recap. Tidy every double sign, gather the positives and negatives, and compare. For a change, do final minus start. For a missing number, use the inverse and check. Now try the practice questions!
